questions.question: When carrying a wide load, a driver should:

options.text: Get special permits and follow special rules, like driving only at certain times.
Honk at other drivers to make them move out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits and follow special rules, like driving only at certain times.
questions.explanation: Wide, long, or heavy loads need special permits. They may only be driven at certain times of day.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe air leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes during a leakage test?
questions.correctAnswerText: 3 psi in one minute
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than 3 psi of air pressure in one minute during a leakage test.

questions.question: A bridge formula:

options.text: Allows less weight per axle when axles are close together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows less weight per axle when axles are close together.
questions.explanation: A bridge formula sets the maximum weight allowed on axles. When axles are close together, the maximum weight allowed is lower.

questions.question: How are hazardous materials labeled?
questions.correctAnswerText: With a diamond-shaped label
questions.explanation: Packages with hazardous materials must have a diamond-shaped warning label attached.

questions.question: At railroad crossings, bus drivers:

options.text: Do not need to stop, but must slow down to 25 mph below the speed limit.
Do not need to stop, but must open the door to listen for trains.
Must stop and check for approaching trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop and check for approaching trains.
questions.explanation: Bus drivers must stop 15 to 50 feet before the railroad tracks. They must look and listen for trains before proceeding. Do not stop only if a police officer is directing traffic, there is a green signal, or the crossing is marked exempt.

questions.question: The center of gravity in a trailer should be:

options.text: At the rear of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep cargo weight as low as possible. A high center of gravity increases the risk of rollover.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks:

options.text: Usually have a low center of gravity.
Usually have a high center of gravity.
Are usually not allowed to cross railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually have a high center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity. Drivers must be careful and ready for the load to shift during travel.

questions.question: Fueling a bus while passengers are on board is:

options.text: Okay, but only if you tell the passengers.
Okay, but only if you are in a hurry.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not recommended.
questions.explanation: Do not refuel a bus while passengers are on board unless absolutely necessary. Never refuel a bus with passengers inside an enclosed building.

questions.question: If a passenger tries to bring a gasoline container onto a bus, the driver should:

options.text: Put it near the back of the bus.
Keep it near the front of the bus.
Not allow it on the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allow it on the bus.
questions.explanation: Do not allow passengers to bring hazardous items like gasoline or car batteries onto the bus.

questions.question: At stops, a driver should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Warn exiting passengers about hazards.
questions.explanation: At bus stops, warn passengers about hazards. This includes warning them to watch their step when using lowered stairways.

questions.question: When driving through a curve during the skills test, what should you do?

options.text: Leave your lane if you need to complete the curve.
Slow down after you enter the curve.
Do not look for other vehicles while turning.
Slow down before you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Before entering a curve, slow down enough so you do not need to brake or shift gears while turning. Stay in your lane and watch for traffic from all directions.

questions.question: When checking your brakes, a slack adjuster should move ____ from where it connects to the push rod.
questions.correctAnswerText: No more than one inch
questions.explanation: Check each slack adjuster after setting wheel chocks and releasing the parking brake. Pull on the slack adjusters. They should not move more than about one inch from the push rod. If they move more than one inch, they need adjustment.

questions.question: On a bus, where should carry-on baggage be stored?

options.text: In a way that lets riders exit through any window or door in an emergency.
In the aisle near the front of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a way that lets riders exit through any window or door in an emergency.
questions.explanation: Keep the aisles and stairwells of a bus clear at all times. Store luggage and freight so passengers can exit through any window or door during an emergency.

questions.question: When alley docking, how should your vehicle be parked?

options.text: With the front bumper on the front boundary line.
With the rear wheels past the rear boundary line.
Straight and within the parking space boundaries.
At an angle and within the parking space boundaries.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straight and within the parking space boundaries.
questions.explanation: For alley docking, first pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking area. Your vehicle must be parked straight within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: If cargo on a flatbed trailer is 40 feet long, it must be secured with at least:
questions.correctAnswerText: Four tie-downs.
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers without sides, cargo must be tied down. Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Always use at least two tie-downs, no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: When checking the inside of a bus, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Check every railing.
questions.explanation: When checking the inside of a bus, make sure everything is safe and works properly. Check that each handhold and railing is secure and safe to use.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning light comes on, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving but have the brakes fixed within a week.
Pull over and check the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the brakes.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning light comes on while driving a vehicle with air brakes, stop safely while you can still control the brakes. Check and repair the brakes right away.

questions.question: Brake fade is caused by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Using the brakes too much.
questions.explanation: When brakes are used too much, they get very hot. This heat causes them to fade, which makes them less effective at slowing the vehicle.

questions.question: What is commonly found in compressed air?
questions.correctAnswerText: Water
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system usually contains water and compressor oil. Water and oil can damage the brakes if they build up in the system. Drain the tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: If you need to sight-side back your vehicle into an alley, what should you do first?

options.text: Drive directly into the alley parking space.
Turn right to position yourself in front of the alley.
Pull past the alley and stop at a right angle to the outer boundary.
Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary.
questions.explanation: For alley docking, first pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking area. Your vehicle must be parked straight within the parking space boundaries.
